the regional organizations of South Asia and Southern Africa have been established in order to promote economic integration and to enhance trade among member states.

the regional integration in South Asia and Southern Africa has been successful in the areas of free trade agreements, customs union and common market, but it has failed in the areas of economic and monetary union and political union.

the regional organizations of the Southern African Development Community (SADC) and South Asia Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) are not as strong as their counterparts in the European Union and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

the relationship between regional organizations (regional economic integration) and their members and how the relationship affects the member states.
how regional organizations and member state relationships are influenced by their political economy and how these relationships are manifested in the international arena.
the relationship between regional organizations in Africa and South Asia, and their member states.

there is no one single model for regional organizations.
regional organizations have a significant role to play in the economic and social development of their respective member states and in the world at large.
regional economic integration in Africa is not as advanced as in South Asia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
regional organizations are a product of the member states.

the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) and the Southern African Development Community (SADC) are both regional organizations that were formed to promote economic cooperation, trade, and integration among member countries.
there are similarities between South Asian and Southern African regional organizations in terms of the economic and political integration of member states.

the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) and the Southern African Development Community (SADC) are both regional economic integration organizations with the goal of improving the economic and social conditions of the member states.
